question: With standalone fact recall established, how do CE versus full-value-vector MSE memories differ in single-hop use and in fresh-mapping MLP swaps without reader retraining?
claim_level: controlled synthetic single-hop behavior; prerequisite replication and bounded extension, not natural-model mechanism or two-hop proof
primary_endpoint: final reader trained on A + same-objective independently fitted memory B; full-vocabulary top-1 over all keys with balanced nuisance contexts
controls: clean exact-key memory readout under both fact-only and actual full vocabularies
final reader + A-memory on A-labels, with held-out nuisance contexts
final reader + wrong A-memory on B-labels; report all keys and changed-map keys
full 2x2 crossing of CE/MSE A-readers and CE/MSE B-memories, with no further optimization
pairing: same geometry, A/B permutations, initial memory parameters, initial reader parameters, training stream, and held-out contexts across objectives within each world
analysis_unit: independent world; three confirmation worlds, not 3072 independent queries
selection: development world only; confirmation uses fixed final endpoint, no B-based early stopping or best-checkpoint selection
boundaries: Moves A.4.5 CE/MSE objective comparison into A.4.3 SSFR task; not a numerical reproduction of the book-author language experiment
Uses author SwiGLU memory with bias, single-head attention, tied frozen embeddings, identity frozen V/O, no residuals or positions, unit-norm interfaces
No expected CE/MSE gap is imposed; equal success is informative about this regime
No downstream task or B labels enter reader training; all failures remain in results
Does not test constrained parameter editing, multi-hop composition, GQA, recurrent mixers, GLM, or Kimi
